newsitem.title: IRAN: Aid pours in for Iran quake victims - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Aid pours in for Iran quake victims - U.N.

text.p: Millions of dollars in international aid has begun to pour into Iran to ease the suffering of victims of the recent earthquake, the United Nations said on Sunday.
The global response to the Iranian government's call last Tuesday for world aid has been encouraging, the U.N. office in Tehran said in a statement.
Nearly 1,000 people were killed, about 2,600 injured and 36,000 left homeless in the February 28 quake which rocked Iran's mountainous northwest region with an intensity of 5.5 on the Richter scale.
More than 920 aftershocks were recorded, the official news agency IRNA said on Sunday quoting the head of the provincial seismographic centre in the provincial capital of Ardebil in the quake zone.

Seismologists on Sunday registered another quake at 3.8 on the Richter scale which they said shook the border city of Baneh in western Kurdestan province. No loss of life or damage to property was reported.

The United Nations said aid pledged thus far included $30,000 in cash and $60,000 in kind from Norway, $35,000 in cash from Denmark, $200,000 in cash from Britain, $300,000 in cash from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, $15,000 in cash and $250,000 in kind from Japan, and $250,000 in kind from Germany plus 400,000 marks from the German Red Cross.

In addition, the International Federation of the Red Crescent and Red Cross had provided 50,000 Swiss francs plus 2,500 tents, 15,000 blankets, 25 tonnes of nylon sheets, 63 tonnes of assorted food items, 3,500 cooking stoves, and three water tanks of 5,000 litres each.
Assistance amounting to $525,000 pledged by U.N. agencies had also been swift and fairly substantive, the U.N. said.
